description.narrative: Stabilization has proven to be the most effective approach to establishing, strengthening, and expanding state authority in conflict environments. Grounded in an integrated programmatic approach with aligned governance and management structures, the success of the Lebanon Cessation of Hostilities Agreement (CoHA) hinges on extending central state authority in Southern Lebanon, linking its implementation to UN Security Council Resolution 1701. Together, CoHA and Resolution 1701 provide the political framework guiding stabilization efforts to support Lebanon’s newly elected government in expanding its authority to the South and Nabatiyeh governorates and asserting a legitimate monopoly on the use of force and enhancing security forces operational readiness. To produce meaningful stabilization effects, a context-specific integrated approach is required for each location, operationalized through three stabilization pillars: (1) increased state-provided security in communities through more effective LAF and ISF; (2) rehabilitating infrastructure and improving service delivery; and (3) providing income support through tailored measures aligned with the stabilization rationale. Within UNDP’s Stabilization Recovery and Reform framework, efforts will align strategically with ongoing local development, security, rule of law, and economic recovery initiatives, ensuring a comprehensive and synergetic approach to stability in southern Lebanon.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
